query: What is your default emotion, and can you change it?
why_in_two_sentences: Neither competitor actually addresses the default-emotion half of the query: the BBC piece is an expert guide to in-the-moment emotion tools (Ethan Kross) and The Conversation covers two-step reappraisal research. Ours defines the default as a configuration being actively held (body, attention, sentence), explains why good news thins within days and the same feeling follows you into a new job, and gives the months-long repetition path for moving a baseline, with 34 FAQs. (The #1 organic result, kinsalecbt.com, fetched as garbled binary, and #3, an NPR transcript, fetched too thin to judge; the #4 result, BBC, was judged instead.)
what_we_do_that_they_dont: Defines the default emotion itself (the feeling you return to once a situation passes), which neither competitor attempts
Explains why good news thins out within days and why a new job does not change the baseline
Names what the default feeling is quietly being paid, the payoff question neither competitor asks
Distinguishes a bad week from a personality from a held configuration
34 verbatim FAQs including the Robbins emotional-home phrasing, emotional homeostasis, inherited defaults, and work-versus-home splits

above_the_fold.ours: H1 is the query, the short answer defines the default and its three components, then recognition sentences; both halves of the query (what it is, whether it can change) are answered before scrolling.
above_the_fold.theirs: The BBC opens with Ethan Kross's credentials and his childhood as an observer of emotion; authoritative, but it is a profile of a scientist's toolkit, not an answer about defaults.

questions_they_answer_that_we_dont: Can distraction be a productive way of dealing with difficult emotions?
Where does the defeatist belief that emotions are beyond our control come from?
intent_mismatch: none on our side; note that both fetched competitors answer the how-to-regulate question rather than the default-emotion question, leaving the definitional half of the query uncontested.
trust_signals: The BBC features a named University of Michigan professor directing an emotion lab; The Conversation's authors are academics writing on their own experiments; ours names no one and cites nothing.
one_change_with_most_traffic_impact: none - ours is the only result answering the default-emotion question directly; the two FAQ additions above would absorb the competitors' best fragments.
